chapter: Connie's Inn, Duke Ellington and the Swingland band
title: Swingland revues, Benny Skoler and Sammy Dyer's productions
summary: Swingland owner Benny Skoler booked acts including the Nat King Cole trio; Sammy Dyer produced revues with a tap dancer, singer, girl line and comedian Dusty Fletcher.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: This was a thing that happened four nights a week on the air, you know, and we played for a great little guy, who All the theatrical people in Chicago know. He recently passed -- and we used to call him the little king. His name was Benny Skoller -- S-K-O-L-E-R, and he -- during his period -- his life period, I should say, owning two or three different nightclubs, he had such people as the great Nat King Cole perform for him with his trio at Swingland. And he

turned out some beautiful performers. They had quite a show there. This particular thing was a production. We had a great producer, and he recently passed. His name was Sammy Dyer, and we would have like an opening number, and then we would have a tap dancer come on. We'd have a singer. Then we'd have what we call a middle number for the line of girls, you know, and these girls could really dance, and then we'd have Dusty Fletcher, the comedian, remember "Open-the-Door, Richard?" routine
